title: Evidence for a change of ASASSN-14ko timing curvature depends on a fixed UV-to-optical offset
abstract: We test a change of timing curvature at cycle 24 in ASASSN-14ko. We use 23 published UV-peak and optical-rise estimates for 19 flares. A Gaussian model includes shared scatter for each flare and separate scatter for each marker. With a fixed marker offset, the likelihood ratio is 14.43 and the simulation p value is 0.001 at the available resolution. With a linear UV-to-optical offset drift, the ratio is 2.63 and p is 0.154. The drift and curvature-change coefficients have correlation 0.842. Only four flares have both markers. Removing the latest TESS event reduces the fixed-offset statistic to 7.08. Thus evidence for a curvature change depends on the relation between the timing markers. The late-flare measurements remain, but they do not by themselves identify a change in the orbit. This is a reanalysis of published timing products, with no new photometry. Tests assume Gaussian scatter, no serial event correlation, and a fixed break. Code, simulations, aggregate results, source hashes and figures are included.
